SUMMARY

Blackstone Inc.(BX+7.82%)reported its third quarter financial results, noting a 10% increase in total assets under management to approximately $1.4 trillion. Management stated that the firm is focusing on secular investment themes, including artificial intelligence infrastructure and the global energy transition, to navigate current market volatility. The company reported establishing significant capital partnerships, including an initiative to deploy hardware financing for technology leaders. Vice Chairman and Chief Financial Officer Michael Chae indicated that the firm expects a significant increase in net realizations in the fourth quarter following a seasonal decline in the third quarter.

Joining today are Stephen Allen Schwarzman, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jonathan D. Gray, President and Chief Operating Officer and Michael S. Which will be paid to holders of record as of November 2nd. With that, I will now turn the call over to Steven.

Stephen Allen Schwarzman:Good morning. And thank you for joining our call. Third quarter of 2020 represented a highly complex environment characterized by an historic increase in bond yields globally including US treasury yields hitting the highest level in decades. Alongside continued geopolitical turbulence, wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, inflation concerns, high oil prices, sovereign debt worries, uncertainty over the US midterm elections, and other challenges. These challenges have continued post quarter end. On the 1 hand, the artificial intelligence revolution is powering robust growth in many areas. While on the other hand, a higher cost of capital has negatively impacted investor sentiment and transaction activity. And triggered significant volatility in the markets.

The S&P 500 index rose slightly in the third quarter with gains concentrated in the largest tech companies and the energy sector. Although most individual stocks declined and the median stock is now 15% below its recent high. Against this challenging backdrop, Blackstone reported strong distributable earnings of $1.7 billion in the quarter. Underpinned by continued year over year growth in fee related earnings notwithstanding fewer realizations as we indicated would be the case on our last call. Inflows reached $63 billion in the quarter. Reflecting sustained momentum across our major fundraising channels and exceeded $270 billion for the last 12 months. The highest level in 4 years.

Most importantly, in terms of investment performance, our flagship strategies outperform the relevant market indices in the third quarter led by infrastructure and our energy holdings. Overall, the unparalleled breadth of our firm and the leading platforms we have established across asset classes have allowed us to navigate changing market conditions. Deploy capital in the most compelling areas, and continue to build value for our limited partners and for shareholders, the firm's underlying earnings power continues to expand substantially and we are moving towards what we expect will be an outstanding 2027. Stepping back, the economy is strong today. The key catalyst, as I mentioned, is the historic level of investment taking place to facilitate the development of AI.

Including data centers, chips, equipment, power generation, construction and engineering services, and many other related areas. This engine is supporting exceptional corporate earnings momentum. As well as momentum in our own portfolio. We also believe we are in the earliest stages of an AI driven uplift in productivity. And consequently, an additional multiyear tailwind for corporate earnings and value creation. Rising productivity over time is also a potential mitigant for inflation. Over the past few weeks, however, we have seen an increased focus in the market on the sustainability and risk of AI related investment. The significant financing needs of companies involved in the AI build out in the context of higher interest rates. And the levels of valuations.

As we have stated before, we believe the transformative power of AI has precedent in the industrial revolution and the commercialization of electricity. And we are in the earliest stages of its development. Demand for compute is accelerating. And we see no signs of that slowing down. As AI use cases ramp, for both businesses and consumers, and the world increasingly engages with the vast potential of this technology. At the same time, there is a critical scarcity of supply. That is only intensified. Seldom my career have I seen such a supply constrained market. Of this scale? Current public attitudes towards data centers will likely only amplify this scarcity.

Over time, as the public comes to understand the advancements that have occurred in data center operations and construction. Including with respect to water usage, and the funding for electricity. These attitudes should change. We also anticipate new laws and regulations codifying these advancements. Will be implemented. Of course, there are risk factors to consider. There will be situations where investors do not have sufficient capital. And projects cannot procure power. Equipment, or the necessary approvals. At Blackstone, we approach investments in this area with the same rigor, and focus on risk adjusted returns that have defined our investment process for 4 decades.

In AI infrastructure, for example, our data center portfolio is built on durable, long term contracts with highly creditworthy counterparties. Overall, we keep coming back to the fundamental supply demand imbalance. Which supports our conviction that this is the right place to invest significant capital As the AI revolution progresses, the rising demand for capital is creating generational opportunities for those with the platform relationships, capabilities, and discipline. To meet this demand. Blackstone has become 1 of the most important capital providers in the AI ecosystem. We started with our data center development business. Focused on serving the major hyperscalers. Which provided the foundation for deep partnership with many of today's AI leaders.

And we have been teaming up with them in multiple ways. We have previously announced the launch of CoreWeave, our partnership with Google, to help address the shortage of compute. We have also created Adept with anthropic. To drive enterprise adoption of AI. And in August, NVIDIA named Blackstone as 1 of a small group of managers to work with them to deploy $500 billion of large scale GPU financing. At the same time, in the energy area, electrification, re industrialization, and of course, AI. Are leading to accelerating demand for power. Following decades of static demand. With 1 of the largest private energy investing platforms, across debt and equity Blackstone, is at the center of this megatrend as well.

We are actively investing across generation transmission, storage equipment, and services and more. In the third quarter, we invested in a leading developer of renewable projects in Europe. And committed to acquire a supplier of components for data center cooling systems. In August, our portfolio company Luminant, which is providing energy infrastructure to OpenAI's flagship data center in Texas. Announced a strategic investment from Nvidia to help fund its development of low cost scale power. And in credit, our energy business backed approximately 15% of solar and storage projects in the entire United States last year. And together with our equity business, has supported nearly 50% of LNG export capacity.

Of course, it is much more than AI and energy, driving our firm forward. Blackstone has established leading platforms to address other paradigm shifts we see shaping the economy and markets. Private credit is becoming a crucial source of financing for the real economy And we manage the world's largest third party focused private credit business. Advancements in drug development are accelerating, and we have built the largest sponsor backed life sciences platform India, continues its ascent as the fastest growing major economy and we are 1 of the country's largest private investors. Private markets themselves remain on a strong growth trajectory. Leading to significant opportunities in secondaries where we oversee 1 of the largest businesses.

And defense is an area that is in critical need of global capital. And we have been highly active here as well. Addressing this need in numerous ways. The firm's positioning across these and other areas powers our deployment fuels fundraising, and ultimately translates to greater earnings for shareholders. The virtuous circle underpinning our business. And as always, the Blackstone innovation engine continues to fire and we are investing today in the leading platforms of tomorrow. Despite the firm's extraordinary record of growth over 4 decades, and our unique positioning in the alternative sector Blackstone's stock along with the other alternative managers has been under pressure. This is due to some of the factors I discussed earlier.

Along with AI disruption, and private credit concerns. Over the past 2 years, while our shares are down meaningfully, our earnings have grown nearly 50%. With commensurate growth in our dividend. In my experience, disconnects of this type do not typically last We have seen similar drawdowns for Blackstone stock before and each time. Our shares ultimately recovered and dramatically outperformed any index comparison. On the way back up. Following the fundamental trajectory of our business. I have learned the most important thing during these periods is to keep our focus on delivering great results for limited partners. Pioneering new markets for investment, and expanding our fundraising channels all of which are occurring now. Our firm has enormous earnings power.

And we expect outstanding results in the years ahead. I believe the future for Blackstone will be remarkable. And with that, I will turn it over to John.

Jonathan D. Gray CIMA:Thank you, Steven. And good morning, everyone. In a world where demand for capital is rising, private markets are more critical than ever. Helping to bridge the funding gap and support continued technological innovation. Steven discussed our unique positioning across the world's most important investment themes, which is driving our results. At the same time, the markets from which we raise capital are expanding significantly. Including in the vast wealth and insurance channels. Meanwhile, in our institutional business, investor confidence in Blackstone remains extremely high. Which is translating to greater capital commitments in many areas, I will focus my remarks on these growing sources of inflows for the firm. Starting with private wealth. Where we delivered another outstanding quarter.

Our total AUM in the channel grew 15% year-over-year to a record $330 billion. With nearly $9 billion of sales in the quarter. Fundraising for our perpetual strategies was up materially from Q2, despite the slowdown in credit. And we launched a number of new products. Our private equity flagship in the wealth channel, BXP, reported record sales in the third quarter of $2.9 billion bringing its NAV to 29 billion in less than 3 years. The largest platform of its kind in the world. Of course, it is all about investment performance, and BXP has delivered achieving an 18% net annualized return since inception.

BREIT grew 9% year-over-year to $58 billion and saw its best regular way net flows in 4 years in the third quarter. BREIT has generated 21 consecutive months of positive returns approximately 11% net over the last 12 months for its largest share class. And BXInfera, reported its highest quarterly sales since launch nearly 2 years ago, at $1.1 billion bringing NAV to over $7 billion. Underpinned by 17% annualized net return for its largest share class. The exceptional portfolio positioning of these strategies continues to power our returns. For BCRED, gross sales were nearly $750 million in the third quarter. Repurchase requests were 10% of NAV above the 5% quarterly limit largely driven by carryover request from Q2.

We fulfilled approximately 50% of total requests resulting in net outflows of $1.4 billion in the third quarter. Investors who requested a redemption each of these 2 quarters of proration received 75% of their capital back. In about 90 days. Another illustration of the semi liquid structure working as designed. Meanwhile, our innovation in the wealth channel is accelerating. Our new perpetual hedge fund product, BXHF, had a strong start out of the gate raising approximately $400 million including October 1st subscriptions. This strategy adds another core building block to our suite of solutions. We also launched a new vehicle outside of the US and invest across our wealth strategies. Blackstone private markets funds, or BXPM.

Which we refer to as Blackstone in a box. And the first 2 funds in our alliance with Wellington and Vanguard went live in the third quarter, including WVB Blackstone all privates fund. Which gives investors in the US access to Blackstone's platform in a single allocation. The opportunity in private wealth continues to expand for the firm. Moving to the insurance channel where our AUM grew 14% year-over-year to more than $300 billion Insurance companies continue to turn to private markets for excess spread. And they are turning to Blackstone for our open architecture multi client model and access to differentiated deal flow.

We have established the largest non captive insurance platform in our industry, including 40 clients in our dedicated insurance solutions area. Representing leading global firms. Of which over half expanded their relationship with us in the past 12 months. Our investment grade private credit platform specifically grew 24% year-over-year to nearly $150 billion This platform is comprised primarily of insurance capital today, but our engagement with pension, sovereign wealth funds, and other LPs is growing. Stepping back, there are 2 key developments underpinning the mass secular shift underway toward investment grade private credit. First, the build out of digital energy and transportation infrastructure is creating compelling deployment opportunities of very significant scale.

Second, large IG rated corporates are increasingly looking to private markets for bespoke nondilutive capital solutions backed by specific assets to support their balance sheet objectives and fund growth. Blackstone is well positioned to be the partner of choice given the breadth of our platform capabilities and reputation. Our recent activity includes large scale financings and numerous sectors around the world, including communications infrastructure and an airline loyalty program in Canada, residential real estate in Australia, and digital and energy infrastructure globally. For our clients, we are originating high quality, long duration investments with favorable counterparty risk all while generating a premium yield over comparably rated liquid credit.

At the same time, our non investment grade credit platform continues to perform quite well. Our flagship funds reported healthy returns in the third quarter, which Michael will discuss. In direct lending, AUM grew 10% year-over-year to nearly a $170 billion despite muted flows for BCRED. Inflows from our institutional LPs remain robust and they are looking to deploy in a lending backdrop that has become more attractive. Overall, our institutional business continues to show solid momentum with AUM up 7% year-over-year. In infrastructure, our dedicated platform grew a remarkable 40% year-over-year to $97 billion. We are approaching the $100 billion milestone only 8 years after launch achieved entirely organically.

Underpinned by 19% net annual return since inception in the commingled VIP strategy. Our multi asset investing business, BXMA, has reemerged as a growth engine for the firm. AUM increased 22% year-over-year $114 billion with record organic net inflows in Q3. BXMA delivered its 20 sixth consecutive quarter of positive returns for its largest strategy. In our drawdown fund area, it was another active quarter of fundraising, We held additional closings for our new private equity flagship secondaries vehicle with over $16 billion raised to date toward a target of at least $22 billion Along with our real estate secondaries vehicle.

We also raised additional capital for our fifth private equity energy transition fund BTEP V, which hit its $8.7 billion hard cap post quarter end. More than 50% larger than the prior fund. This represents the 4th major drawdown fund at Blackstone to hit its hard cap this year. All of which were meaningfully larger than predecessors and had excess demand. And we expect a 5th, our asset based finance drawdown and credit to hit its $4.2 billion hard cap soon. Institutional investor interest clearly remains strong, for high performing Blackstone strategies. Looking forward, we launched fundraising for our new credit energy transition and infrastructure vehicle, targeting a larger size than the prior $7.1 billion vintage.

And we will soon begin raising our 3rd longer dated core private equity vintage. I will finish my remarks today with a comment on real estate. Where we have been navigating a volatile interest rate environment. In the third quarter, we increased valuation cap rates across our holdings in response to the increase in base rates, which led to depreciation in our opportunistic real estate funds. Importantly, while higher rates are a headwind to the sector's recovery, strengthening fundamentals are a tailwind. In 2022, in contrast, when the Fed began its rate hiking cycle, cash flow growth was decelerating across many areas of commercial real estate due to meaningful new supply coming online.

Today, are 3 positive dynamics that did not exist in 2022. First, demand is accelerating in key sectors, including data centers, where we expect a 3x increase in leasing this year across our global platform. And logistics, where our U. S. Holdings saw record leasing activity in Q3. These 2 sectors represent 54% of our global real estate portfolio. Second, new supply has fallen to a decade plus low across many types of real estate. While the cost to build continues to increase A development further accelerated by higher rates and crowding out from the AI infrastructure bill. And third, real estate debt markets have remained resilient unlike in 2022, with the availability of debt up sharply this year.

This does not mean there will not be legacy equity and debt investments in real estate that will face renewed pressure from higher rates, particularly in lower growth sectors. But in this cycle, as with past cycles, we believe we are in a differentiated position overall given where we have concentrated our capital and the quality of our portfolio. In closing, the firm's commitment to our clients is as strong as ever. And we are laser focused on delivering for them. For shareholders, Blackstone remains brand heavy asset light with minimal net debt and a compelling recurring revenue model. And we firmly believe with a lot of growth ahead. With that, I will turn things over to Mr. Chae.

Michael S. Chae:Thanks, John, and good morning, everyone. The firm delivered resilient financial results and overall fund performance in the third quarter. And for the first 9 months of the year, generated double-digit year-over-year growth across fee revenues, fee-related earnings, realized performance revenues, and distributable earnings. All against a backdrop of significant external volatility. Starting with results. The firm's expansive breadth lifted AUM to new record levels. Total AUM rose 10% year-over-year to approximately $1.4 trillion with double digit growth across 3 of our 4 segments. Including robust momentum in private equity and BXMA, and healthy growth in credit, notwithstanding declines in real estate, as we have discussed.

Total fee revenues for the firm rose 8% year-over-year to $2.7 billion Base management fees reached record $2 billion in the quarter, trending on the path we previously outlined underpinned by year over year growth of 13% in private equity and 22% in BXMA. Transaction and advisory fees increased 34% year-over-year to $210 million in Q3, reflective of the continued expansion of the firm's platform. Fee related performance revenues grew 19% year-over-year to $540 million with contribution from 10 perpetual strategies, including BREIT and Real Estate, BCRED and credit, VIP and BXMA for infrastructure, and BXP in private equity. Fee related earnings were $1.6 billion in the quarter. Up 6% year-over-year, equating to $1.26 per share.

Distributable earnings were $1.7 billion or $1.32 per share, underpinned by the strong FRE generation. With respect to net realizations, we said on our last call that we expected a sequential decline in Q3. And net realizations were down 20% quarter-over-quarter. Even so, we were able to execute a number of dispositions, with the largest source of multiple exits in our Asia portfolio. Specifically in Japan and India. Stepping back, the firm has delivered strong financial performance in 2026, despite the year's considerable geopolitical disruptions and market volatility. For the year to date period through Q3, total fee revenues and FRE both grew 17% year-over-year. Realized performance revenues were up 12%. And DE increased 12% as well.

All while seeing positive momentum across fundraising, investment activity and fund appreciation, the key leading indicators of future financial performance. And as we move towards year end and into 2027, the setup is quite favorable. First, with respect to Q4, we anticipate a significant step up in net realizations in the fourth quarter. Including the sales of multiple companies. In addition, BXMA crystallizes performance revenues in the fourth quarter of each year for most of its open ended strategies. With strong returns year to date. As do a number of strategies across the credit complex.

As we look ahead to 2027, expect to return to double-digit year-over-year growth in base management fees, with key drivers including the onset of fees from multiple new drawdown funds in private equity, continued expansion of our perpetual platform, growth in credit and insurance, and the very positive momentum in BXMA. At the same time, the firm's increasingly diversified and scale base fee related performance revenues is a source of strength including notably our institutional infrastructure strategy, which will see its next large scale crystallization of these revenues in 2027. In the context of its remarkable investment performance.

And the surface area for generating transaction fees continues to expand, an underappreciated engine of fee revenue growth for the Meanwhile, the firm's embedded realization potential has continued to build. The net accrued performance revenue receivable on our balance sheet the firm's store value, now stands at $7.3 billion up 12% year-over-year, equating to nearly $6 per share. Nearly 1 third of the receivable in corporate private equity is public and liquid, while the receivable in our private equity energy business has more than doubled year over year. This brings me to investment performance. Amid rising interest rates and significant market volatility, nearly all of our flagship strategies generated positive appreciation in the third quarter, and outperformed comparable indices.

Our dedicated infrastructure platform appreciated 6.4% in Q3, underpinned by continued extraordinary leasing momentum in our global data center portfolio as John highlighted. For the last 12 months, our infrastructure platform appreciated remarkable 29%. Compared to a 4% return for the global infrastructure index over the same period. The corporate private equity funds appreciated 2.8% in the third quarter, and 15% for the last 12 months. With our holdings in Power and Electrification representing the largest gains in the quarter. Overall, our private equity operating companies continue to report healthy underlying fundamentals. Including low double digit revenue growth and strength in margins.

In credit, our non investment grade private strategies reported a gross return of 2.6% in the quarter, and 7% for the last 12 months. Reflecting stable underlying credit performance across the vast majority of our holdings alongside steady current income. Meanwhile, BXMA reported a 0.5% gross return for the absolute return composite in Q3, compared to a decline in the HFRX hedge fund index and 13% for the LTM period. Which was more than double the hedge fund index. The XMA seeks to outperform liquid markets over time with less volatility, and it has done just that. Beating the traditional 60/40 portfolio by 170 basis points per year since the start of 2020.

Finally, in real estate, the Core Plus funds reported positive appreciation of 1.6% in the third quarter, while the BREP opportunistic funds declined 3.2%. Widening cap rates were partially offset by leasing momentum in data centers as well as interest rate hedges. Areas with lower growth were more impacted, including our multifamily housing portfolio. Despite the cost of capital headwinds, favorable portfolio positioning led to positive performance across all 3 of the most recent vintages of BREIT strategies in Q3. Global Asia and Europe. And double digit appreciation in these funds over the last 12 months including 17% LTM appreciation for our latest BREP Global fund. 24% for Asia, and 13% for Europe.

In closing, the firm continues to demonstrate resiliency, and fundamental strength. In a very challenging environment, we have delivered double digit growth across AUM revenue and earnings. And we believe we are very well positioned for the road ahead. Thank you for joining today's call. We would like to open it up now for questions.

Operator:Thank you. We ask you limit yourself to 1 question to allow as many callers to join the queue as We will take our first question from Michael Cyprys with Morgan Stanley.

Michael Cyprys:Hey, good morning. Thanks for taking the question. So the market seems to be reacting to perceived risks from AI related investments. In the context of a higher cost of capital backdrop. So just curious how sensitive in your view is this financing build out to higher rates More broadly, where are you seeing risks here? And how are you protecting your capital from risk of lower than expected returns at the AI complex? I know you have talked about long term contracts, high quality counterparties, but what risk do those contracts not protect you against?

Jonathan D. Gray CIMA:Well, Mike, obviously, it is an area the market is very focused on today. I would start with where we have really focused. Which is on providing compute, which seems to be the area where there are the greatest constraints. We continue to see very significant demand at our companies. Spending it on models is up 20x over the last year. We see all sort of productive uses continuing to expand across our portfolio And we think demand will grow. And the challenge, of course, is chips and data centers and power and amassing capital at scale. And we think at Blackstone, we are very unique because we can provide integrated solutions. We can provide power solutions.

We can provide financing solutions. We can obviously provide data center solutions. And the vast majority of what we are doing is long term contracted. And in the case of the data centers, as you pointed out, these are assets with 15 to 20 year contracts with companies who have $2.5 trillion market caps on average. So I would say for our data center business in particular, the fact that we wait till we have these long term contracts before we put the vast majority of capital on the ground that seems to be a very disciplined approach to deploying capital.

And if anything, all the pushback and the squeeze on capital availability and a bit of the shakeout that we are seeing puts us in, I think, a pretty unique space. The fact that we have expertise and that we can amass capital, we can do very interesting things. it is happening in credit. it is it is obviously happening in real estate and infrastructure. Here for us. So we are aware of the risk whenever you have this kind of large investment boom which is why we focus so much on the picks and shovels.

Why we focus so much on long term contracted assets, why we focus on not doing things on a speculative basis, all of that makes us feel very good. And if anything, as I said, the shortage of compute is growing. And that is making what we build, the entitled sites we have, that are powered, they are actually more valuable today. And I think we will begin to see even larger sites, more concentrated, and more integrated with some of our energy solutions. So we understand that it is a world where people are focused but the CapEx cycle and the need for compute will continue. There seem to be fewer players who can do this.

And that puts us and our investors, we think, in a very good spot.

Operator:Thank you. We will take our next question from Bart Dziarski with RBC Capital Markets.

Bart Zarski:Great. Thanks for taking the question, and good morning, everyone. Just wanted to ask around the private wealth fundraising momentum that you are seeing. We are seeing acceleration in 3 of 4 asset classes. Maybe you can talk through I know performance was mentioned, but some of the key drivers and momentum sustaining into 2027, and an early read on BXPM would be great. Thanks so much.

Jonathan D. Gray CIMA:So the drivers, as always, are the performance. that is the key thing. The brand, of course, and the reach of our wealth team around the world and our relationships That is a very powerful combination Performance and it was in the numbers you heard exceptional performance really across the board. If you look at what we have done in private equity, relative to the marketplace, infrastructure, same story. Real estate, our gap versus other competitors is incredibly wide. In credit, where there was all this talk of some sort of private credit apocalypse earlier this year. Course, of that has come to pass. And so we are delivering for the customers and that is the key thing.

And this market, as you know, is very underpenetrated. You know, investors globally are probably about 1% allocated to private assets. And then to the expansion point, we are. We have got a new hedge fund product that we are excited about, had a very good start out of the box. And it is super early days. In some of these, multi asset approaches. That will take time because it is a new offering. People are used to buying you know, individual products. We are gonna have to educate the market about this. But we have done this before.

When we started BREIT, when we started BCRED the early days, took some time I would expect here the reaction from the marketplace has been positive. But it is gonna take some time to build those particular products.

Craig Siegenthaler:Thanks. Good morning, everyone. Our question is on the evolution of Blackstone's capital markets business. You are still keeping at Capital Light, the HoldCo. While expanding across asset class and geography with investment grade private credit, an increasingly important driver as we just saw in the Broadcom transaction. Transaction. Could you update us on how the business has evolved and how we should think about the long term growth of transaction fees?

Jonathan D. Gray CIMA:Well, I will just start. Do want. Yeah. I would just say, generally, what we see, Craig, is as our platform grows, there is just more transaction activity connected to it. More debt and equity offerings as our wealth business grows, as our institutional business grows, So it. it is it is associated with the overall growth of our AUM and our activity. And we are helping our clients get better execution by using our scale. And then the second component of this is in private credit specifically some of these large bespoke solutions in real assets. Require.

You know, we are using our very large now $300+ billion insurance platform Some of our institutional clients, particularly on the junior pieces, But in some cases, we distribute a bit as well. And so that is growing as that business grows. So we are continuing with this capital light approach. that is what we think is the best way for our shareholders. But we are still at the same time seeing this pretty rapid growth in transaction and advisory.

Alexander Blostein:Thank you. Good morning. I was hoping to go back to the AI discussion and maybe just double clicking to the first question for Mike. Obviously, we have seen wider credit spreads and CDS levels move up for Neo Clouds and some extent, some of the more established players. Can you help us just understand to what extent that kind of capital markets move impacts your own valuation, whether it is on the equity side and things like data centers or anything you guys are doing on the debt financing.

And as a follow-up, I guess, to that, as public markets become more constrained, was hoping you could frame the fundraising opportunity you see across Blackstone to fill some of that gap. Thank you.

So it impacts you know, the multiples a bit. Interestingly, Alexander, on the new assets that you have not yet leased, think you will be able to command a higher yield to absorb this. And you may end up actually in a better spot because it is getting harder to deliver particularly at scale. So we do not really see a massive impact When we commit to these large scale projects, we line up the financing at the same time.

We are very disciplined on how we think about financing this. For the Neo Clouds, I think the key is will they be able to deliver on their compute promises? We have done a number of things in that area providing financing on a secured basis against long term contracts with the biggest hyperscalers We are creating a Neo Cloud but that business is just getting off the ground. The key for those businesses is the deliverability. Compute prices are actually up 50% year-on-year. there is a lot of value in legacy h 100 chips. Before people thought they would depreciate much more quickly.

So for us, you know, in a lot of ways, a world where capital is more constrained and where we have the scale, the expertise, and access to capital. And this gets to the end of your question. That should be beneficial for us. And the ultimate finish product in a world where there is more scarcity of compute should be worth more. And so in terms of fundraising you know, we are continuing to be able to raise capital. Obviously, investors are asking the same questions around AI. But what we continue to see is demand and usage of the AI going up faster than the compute.

And again and again, what we are focused on is what we think of the most senior part of the stack. Either lending or investing against the energy which is a very large area for us, the electrical equipment, and or the. And the data centers that sort of physical infrastructure that is supporting what is happening that we really like to risk return. And if anything, I think the yields will be going up because it is getting harder to deliver that both physically and because of the need to aggregate financial capital to your point, which is getting tougher.
